topic: Schema management stories belong to the Schema Manager
decision: SIMPL-30850, SIMPL-31815, SIMPL-31816 and SIMPL-31817 are not built or tested in the catalogue build. Schema creation, schema versioning (POST /schemas/{schemaName}/versions), the schemaType attribute and the schema forms belong to the Schema Manager component. The catalogue build consumes schemas read-only through a Schema Manager stub (see D29). catalogue-be POST /schemas is not the operation these stories mean. No catalogue test asserts the schema roles GA_SCHEMA_ADMIN or governance-admin.
options: in scope: catalogue-be schema operations, contract to be extended
out of scope: Schema Manager component
basis: The stories say they modify the 'Schema management API' (SIMPL-30422) and are covered by SIMPL-33537. The context CDM schema-manager-be.md owns Schema, SchemaVersion and schemaType. The catalogue-be CDM excludes legacy schema management. sources.yaml lists schema-manager-be.md only as context.
owner_question: Confirm that the four federated search schema stories move to the Schema Manager backlog and are tested there.

topic: Provisional rules for the federated search schema (stub data and owner feedback)
decision: For the Schema Manager stub and as feedback to the owner: (1) schemaType is optional on the version form and defaults to RESOURCE. (2) At most one SEARCH schema may be published at a time; drafts and revoked SEARCH schemas do not count. (3) A new version of the published SEARCH schema itself never gets 409; 409 applies only when a published SEARCH schema with another name exists. (4) The resourceType check (400) runs before the uniqueness check (409); the resourceType clause in SIMPL-31817/AC3 is a copy error and is ignored. (5) Creating a SEARCH schema means uploading a SHACL (.ttl) file plus name, title and schemaType, as for the version form; there is no form-based schema editor. (6) A revoked schema name may not be reused. The stub seeds exactly one published SEARCH schema named FederatedSearch.
options: required vs optional schemaType
409 for any published SEARCH schema vs another name only
one SEARCH schema in any state vs one published
file upload vs form editor
basis: SIMPL-30850/AC1 states the RESOURCE default explicitly; SIMPL-31815/AC3 and the hints say 'another published' and 'one published SEARCH schema globally, regardless of name'; SIMPL-30850/AC1 to AC3 upload a .ttl file. Simplest reading that lets the main path succeed.
owner_question: Confirm the six rules, in particular whether a revoked SEARCH schema name may be reused.

topic: SIMPL-30848 endpoint configuration is out of the catalogue build
decision: Nothing of SIMPL-30848 is built in the catalogue. Trustor endpoints come from the catalogue list (D12): each catalogue carries its Trustor authorityURL, and the Trustor search and detail base URL is authorityURL. No test covers configuring an endpoint.
options: build endpoint configuration here
out of scope
basis: The story note says it is covered by authentication-provider-be and exists only for linkage to the epic.
owner_question: Confirm that the authentication provider owns the endpoint configuration and its role.

topic: catalogue-be operations in the build
decision: Build and test only: POST /self-descriptions/resource (publication with quality gate), GET /self-descriptions/{selfDescriptionId}, GET and POST /self-descriptions/{selfDescriptionId}/qualityAssessmentRecord, POST /self-descriptions/{selfDescriptionId}/revoke, GET /self-descriptions/{selfDescriptionId}/versions, GET /selfDescriptions/quickSearch and POST /selfDescriptions/advancedSearch. Not built: the legacy schema store (GET, POST /schemas, GET, PUT, DELETE /schemas/{schemaId}, GET /schemas/latest), /session, /query, /verification, POST /self-descriptions (service offering), GET /self-descriptions (list), DELETE /self-descriptions/{self_description_hash}, POST /webhooks/schema-events and POST /schemas/{schemaName}/recalcQualityScore. A quality score recalculation is treated as an acknowledged request only, not a business record. In the adapter, the /participants operations are not built.
options: update CDMs and remove extra operations
keep and model them
basis: No live criterion and no CDM concept covers the excluded operations (inventory-review: operations with no criterion); the catalogue-be CDM itself excludes legacy schema and session endpoints. Revoke and versions stay because the lifecycle (D18) and the search tests need them as fixtures.
owner_question: Confirm that the excluded operations can leave the contract, and that recalculation is a request without its own identity.

topic: Search in all federated catalogues without selection
decision: Out of scope. The Consumer always selects catalogues explicitly; the UI has no 'all' option and does not preselect Trustor catalogues. catalogueIds stays required with at least one item.
options: out of scope for now
UI selects all by default
basis: No story offers it and the federated search contract requires minItems 1. BP6.1.2 is a process variant without criteria.
owner_question: Confirm that 'search all federated catalogues' is a later release.

topic: Resource description is the one business name
decision: The business term is resource description in all texts, tests, new operations and new schemas. New paths use resourceDescriptions. Existing wire names that say SelfDescription or selfDescriptions stay unchanged as documented legacy names (mapping in the glossary). The searching actor is the Consumer in every test name and UI text.
options: resource description in new contracts, legacy wire names kept
rename all paths (breaking)
self-description on the wire everywhere
basis: Stories, BP05B, BP06 and all three CDMs say resource description (DDD-01); renaming existing paths would break the contracts the writers must follow.
owner_question: Confirm that SelfDescription paths and schemas are renamed in a later major API version.

topic: One identifier for a resource description
decision: A resource description is identified by its credential subject id (a DID such as did:web:...:DataOffering:...). The same value is claimsGraphUri[0] in a search result item, selfDescriptionId in catalogue-be and catalogue-client-be paths, and resourceDescriptionId in adapter paths. A detail call with that id returns the latest published version. Versions are addressed by version number only through GET /self-descriptions/{selfDescriptionId}/versions. sdHash and resourceKey are not used by the build. The catalogue identifier is one value named catalogueId (catalogueIds for a list); catalogue-client-be GET /selfDescriptions/{selfDescriptionId} requires catalogueId for own and federated details, and the own catalogue uses the configured own catalogue id (E3).
options: resourceIdentifier for the resource and id per version
one identifier (credential subject id), versions by number
keep all names with a mapping
basis: Search items only carry claimsGraphUri, and the detail examples use the same DID form, so a test can pass it on unchanged. The v2 contract marks catalogueId required (OpenAPI wins on the wire).
owner_question: Confirm that claimsGraphUri, selfDescriptionId and resourceDescriptionId are the same value, and that catalogueId stays required for own-catalogue details.

topic: Overall quality score and classification field names
decision: Business terms: overall quality score and overall quality classification. Wire names: overallScore and overallClassification in every search result item of catalogue-be, the adapter and catalogue-client-be. overallCategory in SIMPL-29292/AC3 and SIMPL-29293/AC3 means overallClassification. The v1 names qualityScore and qualityClassification are not used. Inside the stored record the CDM names (qualityScore, qualityClassification) stay; the mapping is in the glossary.
options: overallScore and overallClassification everywhere
qualityScore and qualityClassification everywhere
both with mapping
basis: All entry files use overallScore and overallClassification; qualityScore appears only in the v1 file, which is context.
owner_question: Confirm overallCategory is a typo for overallClassification, and whether the CDM attributes get renamed.

topic: Federated catalogue only means a Trustor catalogue
decision: Federated catalogue means a catalogue of a Trustor data space. The catalogue-be service is called the catalogue service in all texts and tests. The own data space catalogue is the own catalogue (local catalogue retired).
options: federated catalogue for Trustor catalogues only
keep Federated Catalogue for the service
define both
basis: BP06 and all search stories use federated catalogue for another data space; the CDM use is a service name.
owner_question: Confirm the service rename in the CDMs and API descriptions.

topic: The three meanings of active
decision: Resource description: published (stored value active, see D18). Metadata Quality Profile: active Metadata Quality Profile, meaning the profile resolved for the latest published schema version (kept, it is the API path). Catalogue: federation enabled or federation disabled, on the wire CatalogueInfo.active true or false. Trusted, still enabled and authenticated in the stories all mean federation enabled.
options: published / active profile / federation enabled
active for all three
basis: DDD-02: one term per concept; the profile path /qualityProfiles/active cannot change without a contract change.
owner_question: Confirm the federation status names.

topic: Quality Assessment Record representation and part names
decision: The stored Quality Assessment Record is the JSON-LD graph returned by the Quality Scoring Service and exposed unchanged by GET /self-descriptions/{selfDescriptionId}/qualityAssessmentRecord. The structured qualityAssessment in the publication response is a projection of it. The catalogue-be schema names (SelfDescriptionQualityOverallResult and the others) stay as the catalogue read model; their mapping to OverallQualityRating, DimensionRating and RuleOutcome is in the glossary. The threshold source is called the Metadata Quality Profile everywhere (metadata quality definition and Minimum Quality Profile retired).
options: owner names in every API
catalogue names as projection
basis: No rename of existing contracts is needed to build; DDD-13 is met by marking the projection.
owner_question: Confirm the catalogue keeps its own read model names.

topic: Resource type and offering type are two concepts
decision: Offering type is the closed set data, application, infrastructure (lower case) on a resource description (offeringType in search items). Resource type is the Schema Manager open value on a schema; the catalogue passes it through unchanged and never validates it. Since schema management is out of scope (D1), no catalogue test depends on resource type spelling.
options: one concept
two concepts
basis: The CDMs model them separately (GeneralServiceProperties.offeringType vs Schema.resourceType); the search items use lower case.
owner_question: Confirm the two concepts and the lower-case offering type values.

topic: Search scope and main properties
decision: The catalogue selection of a search is the search scope: a list of catalogueId values (catalogueIds). The main properties of a resource description in an overview are the general service properties summary: name, description, offeringType, inLanguage and serviceAccessPoint, plus overallScore and overallClassification for own-catalogue results. The result item is called resource description summary; its wire names are those of the search item n.
options: search scope in the client CDM
API mechanics only
basis: The search item n in all entry files holds exactly these fields; BP6.7.1 lists main properties plus quality.
owner_question: Confirm the list of main properties and the CDM attribute names for them.

topic: Score scale
decision: Every score on the wire (overallScore, dimension scores, thresholds, score ranges, minimumScore) is a fraction from 0 to 1. minimumScore below 0 or above 1 gets 400 invalidInput. The UI shows scores and accepts the minimum score as a percentage from 0 to 100 (whole numbers or one decimal) and sends the value divided by 100. The examples with minimumScore 75 are read as 0.75.
options: 0 to 1
basis: All score values in the entry files are fractions (0.92, 0.91, 0.64, 1.0); the percent ranges in the AC note are a display form. DDD-05 asks for the written UI mapping.
owner_question: Confirm the 0 to 1 scale and the percent display in the UI. API owners (added after step 21): give minimumScore minimum 0 and maximum 1 in every operation, declare minimumScore and minimumClassification as properties of the advanced search bodies, and change the examples (75, 'good', profile ranges 0 to 100, thresholds 70 to 90) to fractions and real labels.

topic: Source and order of classifications
decision: Advanced search with a selected schema: the UI lists the overall classifications of that schema's active Metadata Quality Profile. Quick search and the SEARCH-schema form: the UI lists the union of overall classification labels of the active profiles of all published RESOURCE schemas, deduplicated by label and ordered by lower bound. The backend evaluates the filter per result with the profile recorded in that result's Quality Assessment Record: a result passes if the lower bound of its classification range is at least the lower bound of the selected label in that profile. A result whose profile lacks the label is excluded. Ranges include their lower bound and exclude their upper bound, except the top range, which includes 1. Labels compare case-insensitively. A label that is in no active profile gets 400 invalidInput.
options: one data-space-wide profile
per result, using its schema profile
union of all active profiles
basis: SIMPL-29292/AC3 note (order by lower bound); CDM: each QAR references its profile and labels are profile-defined. In the test environment all schemas share one label set (E4), so the readings agree on the test data.
owner_question: Confirm the per-result evaluation and the inclusive lower bound.

topic: Unscored results and invalid filter input
decision: With minimumScore or minimumClassification set, resource descriptions without a Quality Assessment Record (overallScore null) are excluded. Without any quality filter they are returned. The UI validates the score field (number, 0 to 100) inline and disables the search button while invalid. The API returns 400 invalidInput for an out-of-range score or unknown classification.
options: unscored excluded, invalid input blocked in the UI
unscored kept, API 400 shown
basis: A null score cannot be 'greater than or equal' (AC2); the technical details still ask for inline validation; the contracts define the 400 examples. The struck ACs are not tested as such.
owner_question: Confirm that struck AC6 and AC7 describe the intended behaviour.

topic: Publication quality gate outcomes
decision: POST /self-descriptions/resource calls the Quality Scoring Service synchronously, using the active Metadata Quality Profile of the resource description's schema. Pass: 201, stored and published, QAR stored. Quality failure: 422, not stored, Error body code QUALITY_THRESHOLD_NOT_MET and message 'Quality Score X is below threshold Y.' for the overall score, or 'Dimension D score X is below threshold Y.' for the first failing dimension (scores as fractions with two decimals). Technical failure (scoring service unreachable or timing out after 10 seconds, invalid or unparsable QAR, no active profile, missing threshold): 500, not stored, Error body code QUALITY_ASSESSMENT_FAILED, and one ERROR log line with the resource description id and the reason. Tests check the status, the body and that a following GET returns 404; they do not check the log.
options: 422 vs 400 for a quality failure
not stored vs stored unpublished on technical failure
basis: SIMPL-27998/AC2 and the technical details ('fail outcomes return rejection without persistence', 'Persist only for pass'); the operation's contract lists 422 and 500 with the Error schema (OpenAPI wins on the wire); API-12, API-44.
owner_question: Confirm 422 and 500, the error codes, and that the threshold comes from the schema's active profile.
later_change: error body: problem+json with a code member (D36)

topic: Resource description lifecycle
decision: States: published (stored value active) and revoked. Publication is synchronous: 201 or an error, no pending state, so the 202 response is not used. Publishing a new version revokes the previous published version of the same resource description. Revoke moves published to revoked; revoking a revoked one is a no-op with 200. Search and detail return published versions only. Deletion is outside the lifecycle and not built (D4).
options: published and revoked, superseded becomes revoked
add pending and superseded
keep active and revoked, rewrite criteria
basis: CDM and API enum have active and revoked; BP05B.11 and BP5B.5.10 revoke the previous version; SIMPL-27998 is synchronous.
owner_question: Confirm that a superseded version is revoked and that the 202 response can be removed. Spec owner (added after step 21): add a story for the Provider revoking a resource description and reading its versions, so D18 traces to acceptance criteria; until then tests trace to D18. Process owner (added after step 22): align the BP05B dynamic view with BP05B.05 to BP05B.07, validation and the quality gate before publication with one synchronous answer, and read 'publishes' in step 5 as 'submits' (B-004). Confirm that one revoked state is enough: a revoked version that is not the latest was superseded, a revoked latest version was withdrawn by its Provider, and no reason field is stored (B-002).

topic: Matching rules for quick and advanced search
decision: Quick search: the search string is split on whitespace into terms; a resource description matches if at least one term is a case-insensitive substring of at least one literal value of its credential subject. Advanced search: each criterion is matched against its own property; strings match by case-insensitive substring, numbers and dates by equality or by the operators op1 and op2 of the range filter, enumerations by case-insensitive equality; all criteria must match (AND).
options: split on whitespace, OR
whole phrase
basis: SIMPL-31111/AC1 and SIMPL-31138/AC1 speak of terms in the plural and 'at least one'; SIMPL-31112/AC1 'each search term ... in the property'.
owner_question: Confirm whitespace splitting, substring matching and the per-type comparison.

topic: Search authorisation and discovery access policy
decision: Tier 1: no token gets 401, a token without the role CATALOGUE_SEARCHER gets 403. Tier 2: the User-Attributes header carries the Consumer's identity attribute codes, comma separated. Resource descriptions whose discovery access policy is not met are left out of a result list silently (never a 403 for the whole search). Identity attributes and their federation mapping are owned outside the catalogue (IAA and the gateway); the discovery access policy belongs to the resource description. A missing User-Attributes header on a Trustor operation gets 400; an attribute without mapping counts as absent.
options: 403 vs empty list for a Consumer without search role
mapping in gateway vs adapter
basis: catalogue-be quickSearch lists CATALOGUE_SEARCHER; SEC-05, SEC-06, SEC-20; the adapter contract says the gateway maps attributes and the adapter receives User-Attributes (required header).
owner_question: Confirm CATALOGUE_SEARCHER as the search role and silent filtering by policy.
later_change: 400 for a missing User-Attributes header on all tier 2 reads (D34)

topic: How a discovery access policy is represented
decision: Assumption for the build: a resource description lists the identity attribute codes allowed to discover it; a Consumer meets the policy if User-Attributes contains at least one of them; an empty or missing list means everyone with the search role may discover it. Test fixtures set this list explicitly.
options: model the policy now
leave it to the gateway
basis: No input file defines the policy format; this is the simplest rule that the criteria can be tested against.
owner_question: Provide the real discovery access policy format and where it sits in the resource description.

topic: Own catalogue in a search
decision: Each data space has exactly one own catalogue, so the local quick search needs no catalogue parameter. The own catalogue is searched only when the Consumer selected it. The UI preselects the own catalogue; the Consumer may deselect it if at least one Trustor catalogue stays selected.
options: own catalogue always searched
only when selected
basis: SIMPL-30848 note: 'For each data space there is only one SIMPL open catalogue'; SIMPL-31767/AC1 'from one of the selected catalogues'.
owner_question: Confirm the own catalogue is optional in a federated search.

topic: Catalogue list for the selector
decision: catalogue-client-be exposes GET /catalogues exactly as in the v1 file (CatalogueInfo id, name, authorityURL, active), added to the v2 contract. The selector shows the own catalogue first (configured id and name, E3), then every Trustor catalogue with active true; catalogues with active false are not shown. With no Trustor catalogues, only the own catalogue is offered and the text 'No federated catalogues are available.' is shown. If GET /catalogues fails, the Trustor part is not populated, the own catalogue stays selectable, and the message 'The list of catalogues could not be loaded.' is shown.
options: one selector with own and Trustor catalogues
Trustor catalogues only
basis: The v1 file already defines this operation for the Trustor catalogue list (SIMPL-33471 refers to it); SIMPL-31102/AC2 for the failure; SIMPL-35874 lets the Consumer select the local catalogue.
owner_question: Confirm GET /catalogues is the SIMPL-33471 API and the texts.

topic: Federated search returns one grouped response
decision: When at least one Trustor catalogue is selected, the UI makes one call: catalogue-client-be forwards it to the adapter GET /governanceAuthority/selfDescriptions or POST /governanceAuthority/selfDescriptions/advancedSearch, with catalogueIds holding all selected catalogues, the own catalogue included if selected. The response changes from the flat list to {groups: [...]}, one group per selected catalogue in request order, each {catalogueId, catalogueName, authorityUrl, status, totalCount, items, page, pageSize, totalPages}. To page one group, the client repeats the search with only that catalogueId and the wanted page; other groups stay as they are on screen. When only the own catalogue is selected, the existing local search operations are used unchanged. In a mixed advanced search all catalogues, the own one included, are searched with the SEARCH schema fields. The UI shows one tab per group, own catalogue first, tab label the catalogue name.
options: backend returns one grouped response
UI makes two calls and groups the results
basis: SIMPL-31140/AC1 and AC2 (single response, grouped, paging per group) win over the SIMPL-31142 technical design; SIMPL-35874/AC2 (SEARCH schema when a federated catalogue is selected) wins over the same design for mixed selections. The contract says it does not yet define aggregation, so extending it closes a gap rather than breaking a decision.
owner_question: Confirm the grouped response shape and per-group paging by repeating the search for one catalogue. Process owner (added after step 22): rename BP06.04 (for example 'Consult the search results') and move it after BP06.11. No quality rating happens at search time: the stored rating of D17 is only read and filtered on (D26) (B-008).
later_change: an own-only search returns one group (D33)

topic: Failing Trustor in a federated search
decision: A failing Trustor never fails the whole search. If the call to a Trustor fails (TLS handshake failure, connection error, 403, 5xx, or no answer within 10 seconds), its group has status unavailable and an empty items list; the response is still 200 and other groups are unaffected. A group that searched fine has status complete, also when empty. A catalogueId that is not in the catalogue list gets 400 invalidInput for the whole request. A listed catalogue with federation disabled gets status unavailable without a call. At the Trustor, a caller with a valid certificate but no enabled federation gets 403 from the gateway; a revoked certificate fails the handshake. Both are gateway behaviour (D27) and reach the Trusted side as a failed call.
options: internal 502, Consumer gets 200 with empty group
Consumer gets 502
400 vs empty group for unknown catalogue
basis: SIMPL-31140/AC3 ('empty group ... others unaffected'); the 502 of SIMPL-31113 is the call between the GAs. The status marker adds what F-036 asks without breaking the empty group. The contract defines 400 for an invalid catalogue selection.
owner_question: Confirm the group status values, the 10 second timeout and 400 for an unknown catalogue.
later_change: UI text for an unavailable own group (D48)

topic: Quality in federated groups
decision: Items in Trustor groups carry overallScore and overallClassification as null, and the quality filter is applied only to the own catalogue group; Trustor groups ignore it. Own-catalogue overviews show the overall quality score (as percent) and classification. Sorting of overviews is not built (no criterion).
options: fields removed, filter ignored
fields removed, filter applied at Trustor
fields kept
basis: SIMPL-31140/AC4 (omitted for Trustor groups); BP6.7.1 and BP6.7.2 (quality only for own catalogue). null keeps the existing item schema valid.
owner_question: Confirm the filter is ignored for Trustor catalogues and that sorting is a later story.

topic: What the gateway does and what the adapter does
decision: Mutual TLS, Trusted GA authentication, the federation check and identity attribute mapping are done by the gateway in front of the Trustor adapter, as the adapter contract says. They are not built in the catalogue build. The adapter receives User-Attributes (already mapped) and Correlation-Id and applies the discovery access policy itself (D20, D21). Tests of the Trustor operations call the adapter directly with these headers.
options: gateway
adapter
basis: query-mapper-adapter-be GET /federated/resourceDescriptions/{resourceDescriptionId}: 'The adapter does not repeat gateway authorization'; SEC-10, SEC-13. The contract wins over the story's technical description on where the work runs.
owner_question: Confirm the gateway owns mapping and trust checks, and where the gateway tests live.

topic: Trustor-side search operations
decision: Add to the adapter tier 2 contract: GET /federated/resourceDescriptions (query catalogueIds, searchString, page, pageSize; headers User-Attributes and Correlation-Id) for quick search, and POST /federated/resourceDescriptions/advancedSearch (body advancedSearchRequestPayload without quality fields; same headers) for advanced search. Both return searchResponsePayload with overallScore and overallClassification null, 200 with an empty items list when nothing matches, 400 for missing headers or invalid input, 500 on failure. They search only the listed catalogues of the Trustor's own data space, using D19 and D21.
options: wait for the SIMPL-31880 contract
define it here
basis: SIMPL-31138 and SIMPL-31139 require the operation; the adapter names a separate API not in the input set. Same shape and headers as the existing federated detail operation keeps one style. Paths follow D6.
owner_question: Provide or confirm the SIMPL-31880 contract; align these paths with it.

topic: Schema for a federated detail
decision: The federated detail returns no schema. The UI renders a federated resource description generically: every property of the credential subject as a label and value tree, with the same page layout as for own details. Own details keep the schema-driven rendering. For the search form, catalogue-client-be GET /schemas gets an optional query parameter schemaType (RESOURCE or SEARCH), passed to Schema Manager; with SEARCH it returns a list of zero or one schema. If none exists, the advanced search form shows 'No federated search schema is published.' and disables search while a Trustor catalogue is selected; if the call fails, it shows 'The search form could not be loaded.'
options: schema returned with the detail
no schema, generic rendering
basis: The schema lines are struck in SIMPL-31150 and SIMPL-31153, the later decision of the owners, and the adapter contract says no separate schema is returned. SIMPL-35874/AC3 names schemaType=SEARCH.
owner_question: Confirm that SIMPL-31148, SIMPL-31770 and SIMPL-33885 drop the schema from the federated detail.

topic: Trusted-side detail operation
decision: Add to the adapter tier 1 contract GET /governanceAuthority/resourceDescriptions/{resourceDescriptionId}?catalogueId=... . catalogue-client-be GET /selfDescriptions/{selfDescriptionId} calls it when catalogueId is a Trustor catalogue. The adapter looks up the catalogue's authorityURL, creates a Correlation-Id (UUID) and calls the Trustor GET /federated/resourceDescriptions/{resourceDescriptionId} with User-Attributes and Correlation-Id. It returns the Trustor's federatedResourceDescriptionPayload unchanged on 200, and errors as in D31.
options: wait for a contract
define it here
basis: SIMPL-31153 technical description requires the Trusted inbound and forwarding operations; the only defined federated detail operation is the Trustor side, which becomes the forwarding target.
owner_question: Confirm the path and that the Trustor operation is the forwarding target.

topic: Detail error statuses
decision: Trustor GET /federated/resourceDescriptions/{id}: 404 when the resource description does not exist, is not published, or its discovery access policy is not met (existence is hidden); 400 when User-Attributes or Correlation-Id is missing; 500 when the catalogue service fails. Trusted side and catalogue-client-be map to a fixed set: Trustor 404 gives 404; any other Trustor error, a failed call, or no answer within 10 seconds gives 500 with problem type urn:problem-type:simpl:catalogue:federatedSourceUnavailable and no Trustor details. Missing or invalid catalogueId or id gives 400. The same 400, 404 and 500 apply to own-catalogue details. UI: 404 shows 'The resource description was not found.', 400 shows 'The request is not valid.', 500 shows 'The details could not be loaded.'; no details are shown in any error case.
options: 401 / 400 / 403 at the Trustor
404 for all denials
pass through vs fixed set
basis: The detail contracts define only 400, 404 and 500 (OpenAPI wins on the wire); SIMPL-31150 'must not expose the resource description'; SIMPL-31153 'translated consistently without exposing internal federation details'; SIMPL-33885/AC3 and AC4.
owner_question: Confirm 404 for a policy denial and 500 for a Trustor timeout instead of 403 and 504.

topic: Quality block in own-catalogue details
decision: The UI gets the credential from catalogue-client-be GET /selfDescriptions/{selfDescriptionId} and the quality from GET /selfDescriptions/{selfDescriptionId}/qualityAssessmentRecord, taken unchanged from the v1 file into v2. It shows the overall score (percent) and classification and, per dimension, score and classification. When there is no record (204), it shows 'No quality assessment is available.' Federated details show no quality block.
options: quality in the detail response
separate QAR call
basis: The v2 detail returns only the credential; the QAR operation exists in catalogue-be and in the v1 client file. SIMPL-31143/AC1, SIMPL-31769/AC1.
owner_question: Confirm the QAR operation moves into the v2 client contract.

topic: Consumer search operations in catalogue-client-be
decision: catalogue-client-be v2 gets two search operations, taken from the v1 file: GET /selfDescriptions (query q required, same rules as the adapter searchString; catalogueIds required, at least one item, style form, explode true; minimumScore and minimumClassification optional; page default 1, pageSize default 20, capped at 100) and POST /selfDescriptions/advanced (query page and pageSize; body advancedSearchRequestPayload with the criteria, catalogueIds and the optional minimumScore and minimumClassification). Both always return the D24 grouped response {groups: [...]}, also for an own-only selection, which gives one group with status complete. Routing: when catalogueIds holds only the own catalogue (E3), catalogue-client-be calls the unchanged local adapter tier 2 operations (GET /selfDescriptions with searchString = q, POST /selfDescriptions/advancedSearch) and wraps the flat result as that one group (catalogueId ownCatalogue, catalogueName 'Own catalogue', authorityUrl null, totalCount, items, page, pageSize, totalPages from the local result). When at least one Trustor catalogue is selected, it calls the adapter tier 1 GET /governanceAuthority/selfDescriptions or POST /governanceAuthority/selfDescriptions/advancedSearch with all selected catalogueIds and the Consumer's bearer token, and returns the adapter's grouped body unchanged. The Governance Authority advanced search is built and composed into the adapter root spec next to the quick search; its operationId becomes advancedSearchGovernanceAuthoritySelfDescriptions so it no longer clashes with the local advancedSearchSelfDescriptions. Statuses: 401 and 403 as in D20 and D37; 400 invalidInput for a missing or invalid q, an empty catalogueIds, an unknown catalogueId (D25), invalid paging or quality filters (D14, D16).
options: v1 GET /selfDescriptions and POST /selfDescriptions/advanced in v2, always grouped
the same, but a flat list for an own-only selection
POST /selfDescriptions for both modes, as SIMPL-31142 names it
basis: D24 fixes the grouped shape and the forwarding to the Governance Authority operations but names no catalogue-client-be path; the v1 file holds the Consumer search operations (source hierarchy level 7, used as for D23 and D32). One response shape is simplest to build and test; the local tier 2 operations stay unchanged as D24 says, only the client wraps them. The adapter README states the advanced search draft is outside the root; composing it with a distinct operationId is the smallest fix. API-11 (POST for an advanced read), API-60.
owner_question: API owner of catalogue-client-be: add GET /selfDescriptions and POST /selfDescriptions/advanced to v2 with the grouped response, catalogueIds required with minItems 1. API owner of query-mapper-adapter-be: compose POST /governanceAuthority/selfDescriptions/advancedSearch into the root with operationId advancedSearchGovernanceAuthoritySelfDescriptions and align the tier file versions with the root (1.2.0). Confirm that an own-only search also returns one group, and whether SIMPL-31142 POST /selfDescriptions is this advanced search.
later_change: own-only search can return 500 (D48); duplicate catalogueIds give 400 (D49)

topic: Identity attributes on the search and detail path
decision: The Consumer's identity attribute codes travel in the JWT claim identity_attributes (an array of strings). The service that holds the Consumer's token and calls a tier 2 operation sets User-Attributes from that claim, comma separated: catalogue-client-be on its calls to the local adapter tier 2 searches and to catalogue-be (own detail and QAR), and the Trusted adapter on its calls to its own catalogue and to a Trustor (D28, D30). The adapter tier 2 local searches pass User-Attributes unchanged to catalogue-be. A token without the claim, or with an empty array, gives a User-Attributes header with an empty value, which means no attributes: only resource descriptions with an empty policy list are found (D21). On every tier 2 search and detail operation (catalogue-be, adapter local and Trustor) a missing User-Attributes header gets 400 invalidInput, extending D20 from Trustor operations to all tier 2 reads. Tests of tier 2 operations send the header directly (E1). Keycloak (E1): the consumer user gets identity_attributes ['CONSUMER'] through a user attribute mapper; a second consumer, consumer2, gets ['RESEARCHER'] so policy filtering can be tested end to end.
options: catalogue-client-be and the Trusted adapter copy a named JWT claim into User-Attributes; missing header gives 400
tier 2 services read the forwarded JWT themselves
a missing header means no attributes
basis: The adapter local search summary says policy values come from 'the Client access token', so the token holds the attributes; D20 already gives 400 for a missing header on Trustor operations, and the same rule everywhere is simplest to test. An empty header keeps D21 testable for a Consumer without attributes. The claim name is not in any source and is chosen here. API-60, SEC-07.
owner_question: Confirm the claim that carries the identity attribute codes (identity_attributes is assumed). API owners: mark User-Attributes required: true on every tier 2 search and detail operation, with a description, and add the 400 response.

topic: Publication request and response
decision: POST /self-descriptions/resource takes the signed verifiable credential as a JSON object (application/json), shaped like the federated detail example: credentialSubject with @id, dct:conformsTo with dct:schemaName and dct:hasVersion, and simpl:providerInformation with simpl:providedBy. The resource description id is credentialSubject @id (D7). The schema is dct:schemaName at version dct:hasVersion. The build does not verify the proof. The version number is assigned by catalogue-be: 1 for a new id, otherwise the latest version plus 1; the credential carries no version number. Checks, in this order: no or invalid token 401; no publisher role (DATA_PROVIDER_PUBLISHER, APP_PROVIDER_PUBLISHER or INFRA_PROVIDER_PUBLISHER) 403; body not a JSON object, or credentialSubject @id, dct:schemaName, dct:hasVersion or simpl:providedBy missing 400 invalidInput; schema name and version not a published RESOURCE schema version in the Schema Manager 400 invalidInput; simpl:providedBy not equal to the caller's participant_id claim, or the id already published by another Provider, 403 forbidden; the latest version of that id is revoked (the Provider revoked the resource description) 409 conflict; then the quality gate of D17 (422 or 500). On 201 the new version is published, the previous published version is revoked (D18), the Location header is /self-descriptions/{id}, and the body is SelfDescriptionPublicationResponse: id, status active, issuer, uploadDatetime, statusDatetime, currentVersion and qualityAssessment (D11 projection). A failed publication of a new version leaves the previous version published. Keycloak (E1): provider gets participant_id did:web:provider.example.org; a second user provider2 (DATA_PROVIDER_PUBLISHER) gets did:web:other-provider.example.org for the ownership tests.
options: signed credential as body, schema from dct:conformsTo, ownership from providedBy, 201 SelfDescriptionPublicationResponse
same body, 201 SelfDescription only
explicit JSON envelope {schemaName, schemaVersion, version, credential}
basis: The operation description names schema version, resource version and provider ownership; the federated example shows where schema and provider sit in a credential; D-022 says the root a new version extends is found only in the body. SelfDescriptionPublicationResponse carries the quality assessment D11 calls the publication response. A server-assigned version number avoids a field no source defines. The participant_id claim and the 409 rule for a revoked resource description are chosen here. API-12, API-44, API-60.
owner_question: API owner of catalogue-be: replace the 'type: string' body with an object schema and a realistic example, and return SelfDescriptionPublicationResponse on 201. Confirm the server-assigned version number, ownership from simpl:providedBy against a participant claim (participant_id assumed), 409 for publishing a revoked resource description, and that the proof is verified elsewhere.
later_change: check order and the SHACL schema check before the quality gate (D46), latest schema version only (D47)

topic: One error body format for the component
decision: Every 4xx and 5xx response of every built operation of catalogue-be, query-mapper-adapter-be and catalogue-client-be uses application/problem+json with the RFC 9457 problem detail: type, title, status (equal to the HTTP status) and detail, instance optional. No operation returns the {code, message} Error schema. Problem types: 400 urn:problem-type:simpl:catalogue:invalidInput; 401 urn:problem-type:simpl:unauthorized; 403 urn:problem-type:simpl:forbidden; 404 urn:problem-type:simpl:notFound; 406 urn:problem-type:simpl:notAcceptable; 409 urn:problem-type:simpl:conflict; 500 urn:problem-type:simpl:internalServerError. Publication (D17): a quality failure is 422 with type urn:problem-type:simpl:catalogue:qualityThresholdNotMet, a technical failure is 500 with type urn:problem-type:simpl:catalogue:qualityAssessmentFailed; both carry the extension member code with the D17 value (QUALITY_THRESHOLD_NOT_MET, QUALITY_ASSESSMENT_FAILED), and detail holds the D17 message text. The federated detail failure keeps urn:problem-type:simpl:catalogue:federatedSourceUnavailable (D31). A problem body from another service is never passed through; each service writes its own (D31). Tests check status, content type and type, plus code and detail where D17 fixes them. The UI never shows detail; it shows the texts of D23, D29 and D31.
options: problem+json for all built operations, D17 codes as an extension member
keep {code, message} for publication only, problem+json elsewhere
basis: API-45 asks for RFC 9457 problem details; API-46 and API-47 give the URN form, which the contracts already use (catalogue:invalidInput, notFound, internalServerError). D14, D15, D16, D25 and D31 already speak in problem types; D17 was the only decision on the Error schema. Keeping the D17 codes as an extension member keeps D17 testable. One format is simplest for every client.
owner_question: API owner of catalogue-be: move the shared responses ClientError, NotFound, Unauthorized, Forbidden, ServerError, Conflict and Unprocessible to application/problem+json with the Problem schema, and add the two catalogue problem types for the quality gate. API owner of catalogue-client-be: replace the five problem schema copies (with the stray property additionalProperties) by one Problem schema. Confirm the code extension member.

topic: Authentication and roles per operation
decision: One bearer JWT scheme per service, issued by the Keycloak realm of E1 (OIDC). Tier 1, every catalogue-client-be operation and the adapter tier 1 operations: no or invalid token 401 unauthorized, a token without CATALOGUE_SEARCHER 403 forbidden, also on the Governance Authority searches and the Trusted-side detail. catalogue-be write operations (POST /self-descriptions/resource, POST .../revoke): bearer token with a publisher role, otherwise 401 or 403; revoke also needs simpl:providedBy equal to the caller's participant_id (D35), otherwise 403. POST .../qualityAssessmentRecord: see D38. catalogue-be and adapter tier 2 reads (searches, detail, versions, GET QAR) and the Trustor operations take no token in the build: they read User-Attributes (D34) and the gateway does the rest (D27, E1). An Authorization header declared as a parameter is ignored; the security scheme governs.
options: bearer JWT validated against Keycloak, roles as in D20
OAuth2 scopes read and write as in the adapter file
basis: SEC-07 asks for OIDC through Keycloak on Tier 1; D20 and E1 fix 401, 403 and CATALOGUE_SEARCHER; the catalogue-be operation descriptions name the publisher roles. Plain bearer validation is simplest to build and test.
owner_question: API owners: fix the broken OAuth2Auth reference in catalogue-be, replace the adapter placeholder auth.example.com flow and scopes with the Keycloak OIDC scheme, and add 401 and 403 to the Tier 1 searches and to every catalogue-client-be operation. Confirm that tier 2 reads need no token behind the gateway.

topic: Who may write a Quality Assessment Record
decision: Publication stores the record itself (D17) and does not call this operation. POST /self-descriptions/{selfDescriptionId}/qualityAssessmentRecord stays built (D4) but only a service identity may call it: a bearer token with role QUALITY_RECORD_WRITER. No token gives 401, any other token (provider, consumer) 403 forbidden, an unknown id 404. Keycloak (E1): a service account client quality-scoring holds QUALITY_RECORD_WRITER; no user has it.
options: internal only, not exposed
only the Quality Scoring Service identity
the publishing Provider for its own descriptions
basis: The operation lists 401 and 403 but no role; letting a Provider replace its record would undo the quality gate of D17. Keeping the operation exposed to one service role respects D4 and gives a testable 403. The role name is chosen here.
owner_question: Confirm that only the Quality Scoring Service writes records through this operation, and name the role in the contract (QUALITY_RECORD_WRITER assumed).

topic: catalogueIds in advanced search requests
decision: advancedSearchRequestPayload keeps catalogueIds required with at least one item. Governance Authority searches (quick and advanced): an empty list gets 400 invalidInput; unknown ids follow D25. Adapter tier 2 local advanced search: catalogueIds must be exactly the own catalogue id (E3); an empty list or any other id gets 400 invalidInput. The local quick search keeps no catalogue parameter (D22). catalogue-be advanced search takes the same JSON object as the adapter payload and ignores catalogueIds, because it serves only its own catalogue. 'If no Ids provided no catalogue will be searched' does not apply.
options: empty list 400 everywhere; local search accepts only the own catalogue id
local search ignores catalogueIds
basis: D5 keeps at least one item; the tier 1 quick search already has minItems 1; D22 gives one own catalogue per data space; catalogue-be does not know the configured own catalogue id (E3 sets it in catalogue-client-be and the adapter). API-60.
owner_question: API owner of query-mapper-adapter-be: add minItems 1 to catalogueIds and remove the sentence 'If no Ids provided no catalogue will be searched'. API owner of catalogue-be: replace the 'type: string' advanced search body by the shared payload.

topic: Detail and version list response bodies in catalogue-be
decision: GET /self-descriptions/{selfDescriptionId} returns the latest published version as the stored verifiable credential, a JSON object, as in the catalogue-client-be detail example; 404 notFound when no published version exists (D18, D31). GET /self-descriptions/{selfDescriptionId}/versions returns {totalCount, items}, where each item is SelfDescription metadata (id, status active or revoked, issuer, uploadDatetime, statusDatetime, currentVersion), ordered by currentVersion ascending. It lists every version, including the latest and the revoked ones; 404 notFound when the id was never published. It applies the discovery access policy like the detail (D34).
options: reuse the adapter versionHistoryResponsePayload plus status, all versions
SelfDescription metadata per version, excluding the requested one
basis: D7 addresses versions only through this list and D18 tests revocation of superseded versions, so the list must show all versions with their status. SelfDescription already holds the metadata and is in the same contract; reusing it is simplest. The sentence 'all versions except the requested' is not applied, since the detail and the version share one id.
owner_question: API owner of catalogue-be: give both operations object schemas and examples, and correct the versions description.

topic: One schema identifier in the client API
decision: A schema is identified by its schema name (PascalCase, pattern ^[A-Z][a-zA-Z0-9]*$, as in the Schema Manager stub: Health, Energy, FederatedSearch) everywhere in catalogue-client-be. The path parameters schemaId and schemaName both take this value. GET /schemas returns items with schemaId and name both set to the schema name, plus title, description, version (the latest published), resourceType and schemaType. GET /schemas/{schemaId}/content returns the latest published version. An own detail renders with the schema version it conforms to: the UI calls GET /schemas/{schemaId}/{version} with dct:schemaName and dct:hasVersion of the credential. The search form uses the latest version of the SEARCH schema (D29) and the profile of the selected schema (D15).
options: one identifier, the PascalCase schema name, everywhere
schemaId for content and schemaName for profiles, both in each list item
basis: The profile operation already constrains the name to PascalCase and a credential points to its schema by dct:schemaName and dct:hasVersion; one value removes the mapping a builder would otherwise invent. Rendering with the conformed version shows what the Provider published. API-52, API-54.
owner_question: API owner of catalogue-client-be: give GET /schemas a typed item schema and align the examples and path parameter names on the schema name. Confirm that own details render with the conformed schema version.

topic: Base paths and versions of the three APIs
decision: The build serves the paths as the contracts give them: catalogue-be under /fc without a version segment, query-mapper-adapter-be under /v1, catalogue-client-be under /v2. catalogue-client-be v2 is major version 2 (info.version read as 2.0.0). Tests and the UI use these base paths on the ports of E2.
options: serve the contract paths as they are
add /v1 to catalogue-be in this build
basis: Changing the catalogue-be base path is a breaking change no story asks for; serving what the contracts say is simplest for both writers. API-24 is a should rule and is reported to the owner.
owner_question: API owners: add apiName and /v1 to the catalogue-be server URL in the next major version, and set catalogue-client-be info.version to 2.0.0.

topic: Informing Consumers about a new version or a revocation is outside the catalogue build
decision: BP05B.12 and BP05B.15 (5B.6, 5B.8 second bullet, 5B.9) are not built in the catalogue. catalogue-be publishes no event, calls no webhook and sends no notice when a new version is published or a resource description is revoked, and no Kafka or AsyncAPI contract is part of this build. The signals the catalogue gives are the synchronous answers to the Provider (201 on publication of a new version, 200 on revoke) and the version list of D40. Assumption for the owner: the Provider side starts the notice on that answer, because only the contract side (BP07, the connector) knows which Consumers hold a contract for the resource. No catalogue test expects a notification.
options: Out of the catalogue build; no event from catalogue-be
catalogue-be publishes resource description superseded and revoked events; another component resolves Consumers and informs them
The Provider informs Consumers itself through its own connector after a successful answer
basis: The requirement titles 5B.6 and 5B.9 name the Provider as sender; the catalogue does not know the Consumers with a contract (BP07). No source defines an event, its receiver or a contract for it. Deviates from MSV-03 and ARCH-27 (SHOULD: publish a state change as an event): no receiver exists in this build, and API-62 and API-65 would require Kafka, CloudEvents and an AsyncAPI file with nobody to consume or test them. Simplest to build and test. Keeps D18 and D35 unchanged.
owner_question: Process owner: which party informs Consumers about a new version and about a revocation (5B.6 and 5B.9 say the Provider, 5B.8 says the Governance Authority), and who resolves the Consumers with a contract? If catalogue-be must publish events (for example resource description superseded and revoked, MSV-03), add an AsyncAPI contract for catalogue-be with topic, payload and owner, and a story with criteria.

topic: Revocation by the Governance Authority is the automatic execution of the owner's request
decision: BP05B.13 (request) and BP05B.14 (revoke) are one synchronous call: POST /self-descriptions/{selfDescriptionId}/revoke by the owner (publisher role and simpl:providedBy equal to participant_id, D37). The catalogue service acts for the Governance Authority and executes a valid request immediately, with no review and no request state. The Governance Authority cannot refuse a request and has no revoke of its own in this build: no Governance Authority role on revoke, no revoke on its own initiative. The outcomes stay those of D18 and D37.
options: Automatic execution of a valid owner request; no Governance Authority initiative in this release
Automatic for owner requests, plus a Governance Authority revoke with its own role
A request state with Governance Authority approval before revocation
basis: D18 (revoke moves published to revoked, synchronous) and D37 (publisher role and ownership) already define one call; 5B.8 'Revoke Resource descriptions upon provider request' supports execution on request. No story exists for revoke (P-012), so the simplest reading that keeps D18 and D37 is taken.
owner_question: Confirm that the Governance Authority's revocation is the automatic execution of a valid owner request, and say whether a Governance Authority revoke on its own initiative (for example for a non-compliant description) is needed in a later release, with its role.

topic: Work done before submission when the catalogue refuses it
decision: Registering the connector asset, signing and storing the wallet copy (dynamic view steps 4 and 5) are outside the catalogue build (D4). The catalogue never calls the connector or the wallet and makes no compensating call. On any refusal (400, 401, 403, 409, 422, 500) nothing is stored and no version number is used: the next successful publication of the same id gets the latest stored version plus 1 (D35). A resubmission after remediation (BP05B.06) is a new POST /self-descriptions/resource with the same credentialSubject @id and is checked like the first one. Assumption for the owner: the Provider side registers the connector asset only after the catalogue returns 201.
options: Register the connector asset only after the catalogue returns 201
Keep the asset and the copy as drafts; resubmission reuses them; define a cleanup
Undo both with compensating steps on any refusal
basis: MSV-08 and OWT-A10: each step's failure outcome is defined; the catalogue step's outcome is 'nothing stored' (D17, D35). The steps before it belong to SD tooling, connector, signer and wallet, which this build does not contain. Ordering the asset after 201 needs no compensation and is the simplest saga.
owner_question: Process owner: move connector asset registration after a successful publication in the BP05B dynamic view, or define what happens to the asset and the wallet copy of a refused description.

topic: Semantic validation against the schema shapes
decision: catalogue-be validates the credential subject against the SHACL shapes of the schema version named by dct:schemaName and dct:hasVersion, read from the Schema Manager (stub E4). The check runs after the 409 check of D35 and before the quality gate of D17. Any result with severity sh:Violation refuses the submission: 400 with problem type urn:problem-type:simpl:catalogue:invalidInput (D36), nothing stored, the Quality Scoring Service not called. detail starts with 'Semantic validation failed:' followed by the property paths of all violations, sorted and comma separated. Results with severity sh:Warning or sh:Info do not refuse. Shapes that cannot be read or parsed give 500 internalServerError, nothing stored, and one ERROR log line with the resource description id. Stub data (E4): each published RESOURCE schema version carries a shapes file that requires dct:title on the credential subject (sh:minCount 1, datatype xsd:string). Valid test fixtures carry dct:title; the semantic test omits it and checks status, type, that detail starts with the fixed text and names dct:title, and that a following GET returns 404.
options: catalogue-be validates against the schema shapes; a violation gives 400 invalidInput before the quality gate
The Quality Scoring Service covers it; a violation is a quality failure (422)
Out of this build
basis: BP05B.05, 5B.5.7, 5B.5.8 and dynamic view step 6 give semantic validation to the catalogue as a check separate from the quality rules (5B.5.11 to 5B.5.13). The catalogue-be contract already describes schemas by their SHACL shapes. A semantic error is a client error (API-44), so 400 invalidInput, the same type as the other input checks. Placing it just before the quality gate keeps the D35 order of earlier checks.
owner_question: Confirm that catalogue-be runs the SHACL validation (not the Quality Scoring Service), that only sh:Violation refuses, and the 400 answer. API owner of catalogue-be: document the semantic validation outcome on POST /self-descriptions/resource.

topic: Only the latest schema version is accepted for publication
decision: dct:hasVersion must be the latest published version of the RESOURCE schema dct:schemaName in the Schema Manager. An unknown schema name, a version that is not published, a revoked version or a schema that is not of type RESOURCE gives 400 invalidInput with detail 'Schema <name> version <version> is not published.' A published version that is not the latest gives 400 invalidInput with detail 'Schema <name> version <version> is not the latest version; use <latest>.' This is the schema check of D35, at the same place in the order. The rule applies to a new resource description and to every new version of one, also when the previous version used an older schema version. Resource descriptions already published stay published and searchable when a newer schema version appears; they are not validated again. Stub data (E4): Health has two published versions, 1.0.0 and 1.1.0 (latest); Energy has 1.0.0.
options: Latest version only: an older version gives 400 invalidInput naming the latest version
Any published version is accepted; the assumption is relaxed
basis: BP05B assumption 1, 5B.2 and 5B.3 ('based on the latest version of the schema') and 5B.5.2 (notify about an inactive schema). D41 already treats the latest published version as the one offered. Two detail texts give 5B.5.2 its own outcome inside the one error format of D36.
owner_question: Confirm that only the latest published schema version is accepted, and that published resource descriptions are not validated again when a newer schema version is published.

topic: Own catalogue failing during a search
decision: The own catalogue fails when the call to catalogue-be gives a connection error, a 5xx, or no answer within 10 seconds (2 seconds in tests, E4). Adapter tier 2 local searches then return 500 internalServerError (D36). Mixed search: the Trusted adapter gives the own group status unavailable and an empty items list, the response stays 200 and the other groups are unaffected, as for a Trustor in D25. Own-only search: catalogue-client-be returns 500 internalServerError and no groups; this is the one case where D33's 'always one group' does not hold. UI: on a 500 from a search it shows 'The search could not be completed.' and no results; a group with status unavailable, own or Trustor, shows in its tab 'This catalogue could not be searched.'
options: Same rule as D25 for the own group in a mixed search; own-only search returns 500 with a UI text
Any own catalogue failure fails the whole search with 500
basis: OWT-A10 (defined outcome for every error). D25 sets the pattern for a failing group in a grouped response; an own-only search has no other group to show, so a 500 is the honest answer (API-44, D36). The UI texts follow the style of D23, D29 and D31.
owner_question: Confirm that an own-only search fails with 500 while a mixed search marks the own group unavailable, and confirm the two UI texts.

topic: Limits on the fan out of a federated search
decision: catalogueIds must not hold the same id twice: a duplicate gives 400 invalidInput on the catalogue-client-be searches, the adapter Governance Authority searches and the Trustor operations. With D25 (an unknown id gives 400) one request causes at most one call per listed catalogue. The page size cap of 100 (D33) and the 10 second timeout (D25) stay. Rate limits per Consumer at the Trusted side and per Trusted Governance Authority at the Trustor are gateway behaviour (D27): not built and not tested in the catalogue build, and no catalogue service returns 429.
options: maxItems on catalogueIds plus 429 rate limits at the gateway on both sides
Gateway rate limits only, outside the catalogue build
Duplicates refused, so the catalogue list bounds the fan out; rate limits at the gateway
basis: OWA-API6 and OWT-A06 ask for a limit on flows open to automation; OWA-API4 asks limits with their response. Refusing duplicates bounds the fan out with the existing catalogue list and needs no number nobody wrote down. Call rates belong to the gateway in front of each Governance Authority (D27), which already does trust and federation checks. Deviates from OWA-API4 (MUST) inside the catalogue for call rates only, because the gateway owns them.
owner_question: API owners: add uniqueItems true to catalogueIds in every search operation. Gateway owner: set the rate limits per Consumer and per Trusted Governance Authority and answer 429 with problem type urn:problem-type:simpl:tooManyRequests and a Retry-After header.

topic: Identity provider users and roles
decision: One Keycloak realm. Users: consumer (role CATALOGUE_SEARCHER, identity attribute CONSUMER), provider (DATA_PROVIDER_PUBLISHER), noroles (no role). Tier 1 services check the JWT role; tier 2 services read User-Attributes directly. No gateway is built: tests send the headers the gateway would send.
basis: SEC-05 to SEC-07; D20, D27.

topic: Ports
decision: catalogue-be 8081, query-mapper-adapter-be 8082 (Trusted role) and 8182 (second instance as Trustor), catalogue-client-be 8083, search UI 4200, stubs from 8090 (E4). Plain HTTP inside the test network; TLS is not part of the tests.
basis: Shared set-up for both writers.

topic: Own catalogue identity
decision: The own catalogue has id ownCatalogue and name 'Own catalogue', set by configuration in catalogue-client-be and the adapter.

topic: Stubs for external services
decision: Quality Scoring Service stub on 8090 (POST /qualityscoring/validate returns a QAR chosen per test: pass, fail, invalid, error, delay). Schema Manager stub on 8091: schemas Health and Energy (RESOURCE) and FederatedSearch (SEARCH, published), one active profile shared by all with overall ranges Poor [0, 0.4), Sufficient [0.4, 0.7), Good [0.7, 1], overall threshold 0.5, each dimension threshold 0.4. Catalogue list stub on 8092 for GET /catalogues data: trustorClimate (active, Trustor at the adapter on 8182), trustorTransport (active, unreachable address), trustorOld (inactive). Trustor timeout 10 seconds, shortened to 2 seconds by configuration in tests.
